newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson pulls Swedish shares lower, eyeing Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson pulls Swedish shares lower, eyeing Nokia.

text.p: Swedish shares opened lower on Monday as debt markets weakened and heavyweight Ericsson fell.
At 0825 GMT the general index had fallen 0.38 percent to 3,146.30 in light, summer trade of 254 million crowns.

Brokers said there would not be much action besides the first-half earnings report from Finnish telecoms group Nokia, due at 1300 GMT. The group is expected to show H1 profits rising to about 3.09 billion markka from 1.13 billion markka a year ago.
Sweden's telecoms major Ericsson fell five crowns to 356.5 after losses in New York on Friday.
"Ericsson might move down if Nokia falls, but I think the effect will be minimal and only short-term. Ericsson posted a goods six-month earnings report itself," one broker said.
Truck maker Scania rose two to 227. It is due to post six month results with expectations of a profit after financial items of 1.43 billion crowns against 2.10 billion.
Mining equipment group Svedala rose one to 170 crowns after announcing a new 550 million crown Iran contract.
Bond yields rose in the wake of U.S. data pressuring the interest rate-sensitive banking index down 0.63 percent.
